citations.quote: Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F:M\to N$ be continuous, let $A\subseteq M$ be closed, and suppose $F$ is smooth on an open neighbourhood of $A$. Then there exist a smooth map $\widetilde F:M\to N$ and an open neighbourhood $W$ of $A$ such that $\widetilde F=F$ on $W$ and $F$ is homotopic to $\widetilde F$ by a homotopy fixed on $W$, hence relative to $A$. No compactness of $A$ or its neighbourhood is assumed.
Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F:M\to N$ be a continuous map between smooth manifolds. Then there exists a smooth map $\widetilde F:M\to N$ homotopic to $F$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal F:M\times S\to N$ be a smooth family of maps and let $Z\subseteq N$
be an embedded submanifold. If $\mathcal F\pitchfork Z$, then the set of
parameters $s\in S$ for which the slice $\mathcal F_s:M\to N$ fails to be
transverse to $Z$ is a null subset of $S$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold without
boundary, let $N$ be a smooth manifold, and let
$F\colon M\times I\to N$ be a smooth isotopy such that $F_t:=F(\cdot,t)$ is an
embedding for every $t\in I$. Suppose $F$ is constant near the ends of $I$:
there is $\varepsilon\in(0,\tfrac12)$ with $F(x,t)=F(x,0)$ for $t\le\varepsilon$
and $F(x,t)=F(x,1)$ for $t\ge1-\varepsilon$ and all $x\in M$. Then for every
open neighbourhood $W$ of the image $F(M\times I)$ there is an ambient isotopy
$H\colon N\times I\to N$ such that

$$H_t\circ F_0=F_t\quad\text{for every }t\in I,$$

$H_0=\mathrm{id}_N$, each $H_t$ is a diffeomorphism of $N$, and $H_t$ is the
identity outside $W$ for every $t$. Moreover $H_t=\mathrm{id}_N$ for $t\in[0,\tfrac{\varepsilon}{2}]$ and
$H_t=H_1$ for $t\in[1-\tfrac{\varepsilon}{2},1]$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $V$ be a compact
smooth $n$-manifold with boundary and let $N$ be a smooth $n$-manifold without
boundary ([[def-smooth-manifold]]). Let $F:V\times I\to N$ be a smooth map such
that $F_t:=F(\cdot,t)$ is a smooth embedding for every $t\in I$
([[def-smooth-embedding]]), and suppose $F$ is constant near the ends: for some
$\varepsilon\in(0,\tfrac12)$ one has $F(x,t)=F(x,0)$ for $t\le\varepsilon$ and
$F(x,t)=F(x,1)$ for $t\ge1-\varepsilon$, for all $x\in V$.

Then for every open neighbourhood $W\subseteq N$ of the compact image
$F(V\times I)$ there is a smooth map $H:N\times I\to N$ such that
$H_0=\operatorname{id}_N$, every $H_t$ is a diffeomorphism of $N$
([[def-diffeomorphism-and-local-diffeomorphism-of-manifolds]]),
$$H_t\circ F_0=F_t\quad\text{for every }t\in I,$$
$H_t=\operatorname{id}_N$ outside $W$ for every $t$, $H_t=\operatorname{id}_N$
for $t\le\varepsilon/2$, and $H_t=H_1$ for $t\ge1-\varepsilon/2$.

Let $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a compact interval, and let $X_t$ be a smooth
time-dependent vector field on $M$ such that

$$ \bigcup_{t\in J}\operatorname{supp}(X_t) $$

is contained in a compact subset $K\subseteq M$. Then there is a global evolution
operator $\Psi_{t,s}:M\to M$ for all $s,t\in J$.

Let $X=U\cup V$, where $U$ and $V$ are open path-connected subsets of $X$, let $U\cap V$ be path-connected, and fix $x_0\in U\cap V$. For the inclusion-induced maps in the diagram

$$\pi_1(U,x_0)\longleftarrow\pi_1(U\cap V,x_0)\longrightarrow\pi_1(V,x_0),$$

the group $\pi_1(X,x_0)$, together with the two inclusion-induced homomorphisms, is a pushout ([[def-pushout-of-group-homomorphisms]]). Equivalently, the canonical homomorphism from any pushout $P$ of the displayed diagram to $\pi_1(X,x_0)$ is an isomorphism. No injectivity of either map from the overlap group is assumed.

Assume Countable Choice. For N > r >= 2, the standard block inclusion SO(r) into SO(N) is surjective on fundamental groups. Hence a loop discrepancy of a total normal frame can be killed by a loop supported in a single rank-r orthogonal summand, leaving its subspace and designated corner values fixed.
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Every smooth manifold with boundary has a smooth collar.

For fixed attaching and product-collar data, two compatible smooth monotone roundings of a handle attachment are diffeomorphic by an isotopy supported in that collar. The diffeomorphism is the identity outside the collar.

Assume AC. Let $N$ be a connected nonempty compact smooth oriented three-manifold, and let $W$ be a finite four-dimensional two-handle trace from $N$, with its full external boundary collar fixed. Every smooth framed circle in $\operatorname{int}W$ avoiding that protected collar is ambiently isotopic, with compact support outside it, to a circle in a pushed-in copy of $N$. The target circle may avoid the old finite attaching link. Its prescribed oriented rank-three normal framing is represented, up to homotopy and isotopy of its small tubular attaching embedding, by an integral rank-two framing in $N$ plus the level-normal line. No condition on $\pi_1(N)$ or on the circle's class is imposed. More generally, freely homotopic embedded circles in a smooth manifold of dimension $d\ge4$ are isotopic whenever their homotopy lies in a prescribed relatively compact open set; the isotopy may be supported in that set. Every loop class in a three-manifold has an embedded representative avoiding a prescribed finite link.

Assume full AC. Let $N\cong D^2\times S^1$ be an oriented solid torus in the interior of an oriented smooth 3-manifold, let $K$ be its core with any integral framing, and let $U$ be a small meridian of $K$ with the zero framing given by its meridian disk. Simultaneous framed surgery on $K$ and $U$ returns a solid torus diffeomorphic to $N$ by a diffeomorphism equal to the original identification on $\partial N$. Thus inserting or removing this pair preserves the ambient manifold relative to the complement of $N$, including external collars and boundary parametrizations. An embedded colored ribbon graph avoiding $N$ is fixed. No assertion is made that a graph traversing $N$ is fixed, or that this operation belongs to a complete relative move list.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $N$ be a connected smooth $n$-manifold with
nonempty boundary and let $D\subseteq\partial N$ be an embedded closed disk.
Then the boundary connected sum $N\natural D^n$, obtained by gluing an $n$-disk
along $D$, is diffeomorphic to $N$ by a diffeomorphism equal to the identity
outside a collar neighbourhood of $D$.

citations.quote: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). For every compact collared triad $(W;M_0,M_1)$ there are an adapted excellent Morse function $f:W\to[0,1]$ and an adapted complete downward gradient-like field $X$, both agreeing with the product model on smaller neighborhoods in the fixed collars: $f=t_0/3$ near $M_0$, $f=1-t_1/3$ near $M_1$, and $X$ is its negative Riemannian gradient for a metric that is a product metric there. Here **adapted complete** has the collar-extension meaning of [[def-morse-function-adapted-to-a-cobordism]]: $X$ is the restriction of a complete smooth field on a boundaryless collar extension of $W$; a trajectory is followed in $W$ only until it exits a face.

be an embedded submanifold. If $\mathcal F\pitchfork Z$, then the set of
parameters $s\in S$ for which the slice $\mathcal F_s:M\to N$ fails to be
transverse to $Z$ is a null subset of $S$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Every open cover of a smooth manifold with boundary admits a smooth partition of unity subordinate to it.

Let $M$ be a smooth manifold, let $K\subseteq M$ be compact, and let $W\subseteq M$ be open with $K\subseteq W$. Then there exists a smooth function $\rho:M\to [0,1]$ that equals $1$ on an open neighbourhood of $K$ and satisfies $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)\subseteq W$.

Let $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a compact interval, and let $X_t$ be a smooth
time-dependent vector field on $M$ such that

$$ \bigcup_{t\in J}\operatorname{supp}(X_t) $$

is contained in a compact subset $K\subseteq M$. Then there is a global evolution
operator $\Psi_{t,s}:M\to M$ for all $s,t\in J$.

Let $X$ be a smooth vector field on $M$. For each $p\in M$, let
$\gamma_p:I_p\to M$ be the maximal integral curve through $p$, and set

$$ \mathcal D:=\{(t,p)\in\mathbb R\times M:t\in I_p\}, \qquad \Phi(t,p):=\gamma_p(t). $$

Then $\mathcal D$ is open in $\mathbb R\times M$, each fibre $\mathcal D_p$ is
an interval containing $0$, the map $\Phi:\mathcal D\to M$ is smooth, and
$\Phi$ is the unique maximal local flow generated by $X$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $(W;M_0,M_1)$ be a compact triad and let $f$ be
an adapted Morse function whose critical points of index $k$ all lie at one
level $c\in(0,1)$, with no critical point of another index at $c$ and no other
critical value in a neighbourhood of $c$. Then the
sublevel just above $c$ is obtained from the sublevel just below $c$ by
attaching disjoint $k$-handles, one for each index-$k$ critical point.
Equivalently, handles of equal index attached at one level may be regarded as
attached simultaneously or successively in any order, the result being the same
up to diffeomorphism fixing the incoming face and respecting the lower sublevel up to homotopy of pairs. On the common attached-stage model, reordering disjoint attachments fixes its entire lower stage. Handles of equal index may
be reordered freely, and attaching embeddings may be changed by isotopy of the
attaching region.

For fixed attaching and product-collar data, two compatible smooth monotone roundings of a handle attachment are diffeomorphic by an isotopy supported in that collar. The diffeomorphism is the identity outside the collar.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $f$ be adapted on a compact triad with adapted
field $X$, and let $P$ (value $c$) and $Q$ (value $c'>c$) be consecutive
critical levels such that $\operatorname{ind}(p)\ge\operatorname{ind}(q)$ for
all $p\in P$, $q\in Q$. Let $U$ be a prescribed neighbourhood of a regular level
$f^{-1}(v)$ with $c<v<c'$. Then there is a complete adapted downward
gradient-like field $X'$ for $f$, equal to $X$ outside $U$, such that for all
$q\in Q$ and $p\in P$ the crossing spheres $A_q$ and $B_p$ of the previous
lemma are pairwise disjoint.

Consequently no trajectory of $X'$ has one limit in $P$ and the other in $Q$,
and the corresponding compact trajectory sets are disjoint. The field change may be chosen arbitrarily small in $C^\infty$ on $W$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $(f,X)$ be adapted on a compact triad, and choose regular $0<u<c<c'<v<1$ such that the critical set in $K=f^{-1}[u,v]$ consists exactly of finite clusters $P,Q$ at values $c,c'$. Suppose there is no $X$-trajectory from a point of $Q$ to a point of $P$. Then for any $a,a'\in(u,v)$, including $a>a'$ or $a=a'$, there is an adapted Morse $g$ with the same critical points and indices as $f$, $g=a$ on $P$, $g=a'$ on $Q$, and $X$ still downward gradient-like for $g$. The function is $f$ outside the interior of $K$ and near its two end levels, and is $f$ plus a constant near every critical point. On a triad with just these two critical clusters, one may also use its face levels as $u,v$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $(W;M_0,M_1)$ be a nonempty compact connected triad with
$M_0\ne\varnothing$ connected. Then $W$ admits a handle decomposition relative
to $M_0$ with no $0$-handles. If $M_0$ has $k$ components the same argument
leaves no $0$-handles and begins with $k-1$ connecting $1$-handles; if
$M_0=\varnothing$, exactly the $0$-handles needed to create the components of
$W$ remain, one per component.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $N$ be a connected smooth $n$-manifold with
nonempty boundary and let $D\subseteq\partial N$ be an embedded closed disk.
Then the boundary connected sum $N\natural D^n$, obtained by gluing an $n$-disk
along $D$, is diffeomorphic to $N$ by a diffeomorphism equal to the identity
outside a collar neighbourhood of $D$.

Assume AC. Every compact closed oriented smooth three-manifold $X$ admits a compact oriented smooth four-manifold $W$ and an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism $j:\partial W\to X$. Disconnected and empty manifolds are included. Consequently $\Omega_3^{SO}=0$ integrally, with a single copy of each input manifold.

More precisely, if $X=M\cup C$ is an actual closed manifold obtained by attaching specified smooth caps $C$ to a compact oriented three-manifold $M$ along specified collared boundary parametrizations, the identification $j$ retains these marked submanifolds, their parametrizations and any decorations by pullback. No extension of a boundary diffeomorphism across a cap or filling is required. The assertion is existence; a simultaneous choice of fillings for a set of inputs may use AC and is not asserted canonical.

Assume AC. Let $d\ge4$, and let $V$ be a compact smooth $d$-dimensional bordism with corners, horizontal faces $A_0,A_1$, and vertical face $B\times[0,1]$, with compatible product collar charts fixed. Here $\partial A_i=B\times\{i\}$. There are excellent Morse data with all critical points interior, equal to the specified height $t$ on a fixed smaller vertical product collar, zero and one on the horizontal faces with their prescribed inward collar models. They give a finite handle decomposition whose attaching thickenings lie in the interiors of horizontal levels, away from the fixed vertical collar, retaining the actual outgoing identification. Critical values may be ordered by index while this entire boundary height is fixed. If $V,A_0,A_1$ are connected and $A_0,A_1$ are nonempty, there is such a relative presentation with no handles of index zero or $d$. No fundamental-group assumption or h-cobordism hypothesis is imposed.

Assume AC. In dimension $d\ge4$, a one-handle whose feet lie in the same connected lower stage can be replaced, by an interior framed circle surgery, with one $(d-2)$-handle. The resulting manifold may change, but its entire boundary, specified collar and every later attaching map are identified with the old ones. The framing for this existence trade is the displayed product framing. Separately, surgery on a prescribed rank-three-framed circle lying in a product three-dimensional level of an oriented four-manifold, with its framing homotopic to a level rank-two framing plus the level-normal line, is represented relative to the unaffected boundary by adjoining two four-dimensional two-handles on that framed knot $K$ and a small disk-framed zero meridian $U$. The statement retains the integral framing of $K$. In a two-handle trace every interior framed circle can be put in this form by the preceding circle lemma. The pair's boundary identification is the boundary-relative local O3 identification.

Assume AC. Let $Y$ be a closed oriented smooth three-manifold and let $W_0,W_1$ be compact oriented smooth four-manifolds, with $W_0$ nonempty, with fixed collars and orientation-preserving parametrizations $\phi_i:\partial W_i\to Y$. Form the actual closed seam $M=(-W_0)\cup_YW_1$ using $\phi_1^{-1}\phi_0$, and put $s=\sigma(M)$. Let $W_0'$ be its interior connected sum with $s$ complex-oriented projective planes for $s\ge0$, or $-s$ oppositely oriented projective planes for $s<0$, using balls away from its boundary collar.
